analysis.title: 10 Charts We're Talking About
key_insights: Largest standardized cross-asset movers point to three cross-currents for risk: the AI hardware/infrastructure debate after the midterm results, weakness in energy prices, and a hotter than expected CPI that adds pressure on the Fed for more or quicker hikes.
Winners on the standardized screen are the USD versus oil exporters or safe havens. Losers are the more levered pockets of credit and front-end USD rates.

Hyperscalers look well positioned: owners of existing power and compute capacity gain leverage as new supply becomes harder to build, and independent model developers and cloud intermediaries depend on access to that infrastructure. Owners can keep renting capacity externally or allocate more to their own models.

The neocloud complex is more exposed. Operators that own land, power and shell have leverage and can generate value for equity holders even if they hit trouble. Operators with only leases are middlemen in a business model that requires operational perfection (Chamath Palihapitiya, GS Top of Mind).
Pressure on neoclouds may be compounded by pain in NVDA, described as the 'central bank of AI'.

GS analyst Jim Schneider's first take on NVDA draws an analogy to Apple in 2011 after Steve Jobs' leave of absence and death. Apple de-rated from ~17X to ~12X NTM P/E over ~18 months, fell to ~9X in 2013, then recovered to ~15X. GS expects NVDA to search for the right multiple until leadership and business momentum are clearer, and sees the current price as favorable risk/reward given ~80% expected EPS growth.

A NY Times pre-midterm poll shows voters are less focused on data centers than the market seems to be, but 'economy' ranks highest as the most important issue, and AI-led growth ties the economy closely to the infrastructure buildout.

GS economists estimate wealth effects added more than 0.4pp to annualized 2026 consumption growth as equities rose in H1. With home prices roughly flat in the forecast, next year's impulse hinges on equities.
Trump's post on the morning of 12 Nov reinforces the status quo and the maintenance of a blockade, which GS ties to the energy cross-current.
The Dec 11 government spending deadline (including military) may be the next political milestone, with a risk that Democrats seek to address the Iran war in the negotiations.
Bond bulls want the Fed to look through the hot CPI prints because energy prices are lower. Further Middle East escalation, or no resolution, may limit the Fed's ability to do so.

GS economists expect inflation to be meaningfully lower by end 2027 but think the recent prints will lead most FOMC participants to signal a third hike in the December dot plot, and a firmer January inflation report would make delivering it the path of least resistance even if the energy shock has ended by then.
GS added a third 25bp hike to its forecast for March 2027 and left the terminal fed funds forecast unchanged at 3.25-3.5%.

Praneet Shah (Global Head of FX Options Trading) frames the conflict as a binding constraint for the Fed. If signs improve in coming months, the bottom right quadrant of his framework unlocks, with dispersion among winners and a tilt toward those with stronger balance sheets.

market_movers.rationale: Jim Schneider sees the current price as favorable risk/reward given ~80% expected EPS growth, while expecting a multiple search until leadership and momentum are clearer. The Buy rating is not stated in this note.

sector_views.rationale: Owners of existing power and compute capacity gain leverage as new supply becomes harder to build.
Operators that only lease capacity are middlemen with obligations and take-or-pay commitments to service. Operators owning land, power and shell are better placed.

earnings_insights: GS expects NVDA to deliver ~80% EPS growth (GS estimates, no period stated in the note).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Adds pressure on the Fed for more or quicker hikes. The report does not give the numeric print.
Unchanged, even with a third 25bp hike added.
Most FOMC participants are expected to signal a third hike in the December dot plot, and a firmer January inflation report would make it the path of least resistance.
Next year's impulse depends on equities, since home prices are roughly flat in the GS forecast.

risk_factors: Further Middle East escalation or no resolution to the conflict could limit the Fed's ability to look through hot CPI.
Neocloud obligations and take-or-pay commitments may exceed revenue capacity for lease-only operators.
NVDA leadership uncertainty and a possible de-rating, as in the Apple 2011-2013 analog.
Equity declines would reduce the wealth-effect support for 2027 consumption.
Dec 11 government funding deadline could become entangled with the Iran war.
